note: The only list of what the site publishes. A campaign's runs are read from results/<id>/ (its campaign.json and one directory per run); a campaign published before campaigns existed names its one run directory instead. results/dev is never published. Add "featured": "<id>" to choose the campaign the site opens on; without it, the site opens on the newest complete campaign (D58). Each campaign also carries the words the site shows for it (D93): "title" (snake_case, at most four words), "answer" (one or two plain sentences, each of at most 25 words), "whys" (spec name to why it is in the campaign, at most twelve words; an empty string removes the definition's), "labels" (spec name to a short name of at most four words), only where the definition's question has jargon, "question" (the wording shown instead; the definition file is never edited), and on the featured campaign "featured_spec" (the spec About's card leads with).

campaigns.title: baseline
campaigns.question: How many microVMs fit on one m8i.4xlarge?
campaigns.answer: One m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) held 8 microVMs of 2 vCPU / 2 GiB, 0.50 microVMs per host vCPU; 12 failed. Host CPU ran out first; 9–11 were not tried.

whys.baseline: The starting point for every later campaign

notes: Tasks start as soon as every microVM is ready.

campaigns.title: m8i_host_size
campaigns.answer: Close: m8i.4xlarge (16 vCPUs) held 9 microVMs on both replicas and m8i.2xlarge (8 vCPUs) held 4, 0.56 against 0.50 microVMs per host vCPU. Host CPU ran out first on every host.

whys.m8i-4xlarge: The same host as the baseline campaign
whys.m8i-2xlarge: Half the vCPUs of the same family

campaigns.title: host_memory
campaigns.answer: No: with 4 GiB microVMs, c8i.4xlarge (32 GiB) held 9 microVMs on both replicas and m8i.4xlarge (64 GiB) held 9 and 8. Host CPU ran out first on every host, never memory.

whys.m8i-4xlarge: The 16-vCPU host again, with 64 GiB of memory
whys.c8i-4xlarge: The same vCPUs with half the memory, 32 GiB

campaigns.title: hypervisor
campaigns.answer: Yes: Cloud Hypervisor and Firecracker each held 9 microVMs on both m8i.4xlarge replicas; Firecracker with MMIO devices and no random-number device held 8 and 9. Host CPU ran out first every time.

whys.firecracker: Firecracker set up with the same devices as Cloud Hypervisor
whys.firecracker-mmio: Firecracker with the baseline's MMIO devices

campaigns.title: metal_host
campaigns.answer: One m8i.metal-48xl held at least 192 microVMs, 1.0 microVMs per host vCPU, one burst costing $0.216–0.221 per 1,000 tasks; every density passed. It was judged at the design's step targets, with task p95 within 5 s and ready within 900 s; the harness caps a host at 200.
notes: Its step targets are the design's (p50 within 2 s, p95 within 3 s), not the nested campaigns' 1 s and 2 s.
Every density passed. A host runs at most 200 microVMs in this harness, so the limit is above 192.

campaigns.title: metal_host_tight_slo
campaigns.question: At the nested campaigns' step targets (p50 within 1 s, p95 within 2 s), how many microVMs fit on a metal host?
campaigns.answer: One m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) held 140 microVMs at $0.121–0.126 per 1,000 tasks, 0.73 microVMs per host vCPU against 0.56 on a nested m8i.4xlarge. Host CPU ran out first at 144.

whys.firecracker-metal: The metal host again, held to the nested campaigns' step targets

notes: The same SLO as the nested campaigns: each step's p50 within 1 s and p95 within 2 s.
Densities are close together between 128 and 144, around where hv-host-2's trials would have crossed this SLO.

campaigns.title: small_c8i_hosts
campaigns.answer: Only the smallest did: c8i.xlarge held 2 microVMs at $0.105–0.111 per 1,000 tasks, against $0.117–0.147 on the larger hosts, all 0.50–0.56 microVMs per host vCPU. Host CPU ran out first everywhere: c8i.2xlarge held 4, c8i.4xlarge 8–9, m8i.4xlarge 9.

whys.m8i-4xlarge: 2 vCPU / 2 GiB on m8i.4xlarge, for comparison
whys.c8i-4xlarge: The same vCPUs as m8i.4xlarge at a lower price
whys.c8i-xlarge: A quarter of the vCPUs of c8i.4xlarge

campaigns.title: microvm_size_cold
campaigns.answer: No, not started cold: on c8i.xlarge, 1-vCPU microVMs held 2 and 1 against 2 for 2-vCPU, one burst costing $0.148–0.288 against $0.137–0.140 per 1,000 tasks. With 1 vCPU the host was never full; each microVM's own vCPU was busy starting up.

whys.c8i-xlarge: 2 vCPU / 2 GiB on c8i.xlarge, for comparison
whys.c8i-xlarge-1vcpu: One vCPU per microVM instead of two
whys.m8i-4xlarge: The larger host from earlier campaigns, for comparison

campaigns.title: microvm_size_warm
campaigns.answer: No: over the microVM's whole life, 2-vCPU microVMs cost $0.108–0.120 per 1,000 tasks against $0.100–0.105 for 1 vCPU / 1 GiB. Warm, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB microVMs held 4 on c8i.xlarge, 1.0 microVMs per host vCPU; host CPU ran out.

whys.c8i-xlarge: 2 vCPU / 2 GiB on c8i.xlarge, now with a warm start
whys.c8i-xlarge-1vcpu: One vCPU per microVM instead of two
whys.c8i-xlarge-1vcpu-1gib: One vCPU and half the memory per microVM
whys.m8i-4xlarge: The larger host from earlier campaigns, for comparison

campaigns.title: chromium_no_preload
campaigns.answer: Yes: without the preload c8i.xlarge held 3–4 microVMs instead of 2, at $0.092–0.106 instead of $0.105–0.109 per 1,000 tasks. On m8i.4xlarge it held 13 instead of 9, at $0.130–0.134 instead of $0.144–0.149; host CPU ran out first everywhere.

whys.c8i-xlarge: 2 vCPU / 2 GiB on c8i.xlarge, for comparison
whys.c8i-xlarge-nopre: The same spec with the omnibox preload turned off
whys.m8i-4xlarge: The larger host from earlier campaigns, for comparison
whys.m8i-4xlarge-nopre: The larger host with the omnibox preload turned off

campaigns.title: metal_chromium_no_preload
campaigns.question: Does headless Chromium without its omnibox preload fit more microVMs on a metal host?
campaigns.answer: Yes: without the preload one m8i.metal-48xl (192 vCPUs) held at least 200 microVMs (the harness's cap), 1.04 microVMs per host vCPU. With it the same spec held 140 (metal_host_tight_slo); one burst fell from $0.218–0.219 to $0.182–0.190 per 1,000 tasks.

whys.firecracker-metal-nopre: The metal host again, with the omnibox preload turned off

campaigns.title: guest_boot_tuning
campaigns.question: Do a quiet guest console and huge pages cut CPU per task on headless Chromium without its omnibox preload?
campaigns.answer: Huge pages moved c8i.xlarge from 3 microVMs to 5–6, cutting cost from $0.089–0.092 to $0.063–0.074 per 1,000 tasks; a quiet console held 3 at $0.081–0.083. With both, the 1 vCPU / 1 GiB guest held 6 at $0.038–0.047 (host CPU ran out); m8i.4xlarge rose from 13 to at least 18.

whys.c8i-xlarge-quiet: The guest boots without console output or a keyboard probe
whys.c8i-xlarge-stack: Both changes together on a smaller microVM
whys.m8i-4xlarge-lean: The larger host, guest unchanged, for comparison
whys.m8i-4xlarge-thp: Huge pages alone on the larger host

campaigns.title: tuned_guest_warm_start
campaigns.question: With a 5 s warm start, is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task than a 2 vCPU / 2 GiB microVM?
campaigns.answer: Yes: warm, the tuned guest held 6 microVMs on c8i.xlarge at $0.039–0.049 per 1,000 tasks, against 4 at $0.103–0.107 for 2 vCPU / 2 GiB. Plain 1 vCPU / 1 GiB microVMs held 4–5 at $0.076–0.081; host CPU ran out first, and cold the tuned guest also held 6.

whys.c8i-xlarge-lean: The spec the tuned guest has to beat
whys.c8i-xlarge-1vcpu-1gib-lean: The smaller microVM alone, without the guest tuning
whys.c8i-xlarge-stack: The smaller microVM with a quiet console and huge pages
whys.m8i-4xlarge-lean: The larger host from earlier campaigns, for comparison

campaigns.title: tuned_guest_host_size
campaigns.question: Is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task on a 4-vCPU or a 16-vCPU c8i host?
campaigns.answer: The 4-vCPU host is cheaper: c8i.xlarge held 6–7 microVMs at $0.038–0.047 per 1,000 tasks, c8i.4xlarge 25–28 at $0.046–0.053. Host CPU ran out first on both.

whys.c8i-xlarge-stack: The tuned guest on the 4-vCPU host
whys.c8i-4xlarge-stack: The same tuned guest on a 16-vCPU host
whys.m8i-4xlarge-lean: The 16-vCPU host from earlier campaigns, for comparison

campaigns.title: tuned_guest_metal
campaigns.question: Is the tuned guest (1 vCPU / 1 GiB, no omnibox preload, a quiet console, huge pages) cheaper per task on a metal host than on c8i.xlarge?
campaigns.answer: No: on m8i.metal-48xl the tuned guest held at least 200 microVMs; one burst cost $0.163–0.165 per 1,000 tasks against $0.039–0.049 on c8i.xlarge. With 4 KiB pages it held 192 at $0.178–0.187 per 1,000 tasks, host CPU running out at 200; the harness caps a host at 200.
